title: Representation Learning for Sample-Efficient CATE Estimation by Leveraging Multiple Outcomes
abstract: arXiv:2609.06294v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Estimating conditional average treatment effects (CATE) enables efficient targeting of interventions, but many applications have limited experimental samples, making it difficult to estimate heterogeneous effects from high-dimensional covariates. In such settings, policymakers and medical practitioners often succumb to the curse of dimensionality or apply off-the-shelf dimension reduction methods that may not preserve treatment heterogeneity. Yet these domains often come with large historical datasets measuring a wide range of outcomes -- a source of supervision that is rarely exploited in practice. Following causal representation learning, we hypothesize that such domains with high-dimensional covariates have lower-dimensional underlying dynamics. translated_title: 通过利用多个结果实现样本高效CATE估计的表示学习
translated_abstract: 估计条件平均处理效应（CATE）能够实现对干预措施的高效目标定位，但许多应用的实验样本有限，使得从高维协变量中估计异质性效应变得困难。在这种情况下，政策制定者和医疗从业者往往陷入维度灾难，或使用可能无法保留处理异质性的现成降维方法。然而，这些领域通常拥有大量测量了广泛结果的历史数据集——这是一个在实践中很少被利用的监督信号来源。遵循因果表示学习的思路，我们假设这类具有高维协变量的领域存在低维的底层动态。因此，我们可以利用历史数据中测量的多样化结果来学习协变量的低维表示。在理论方面，我们证明了当辅助结果...
tldr: 该论文提出利用历史数据中丰富的多结果测量信息，通过因果表示学习将高维协变量降维到保留处理效应异质性的低维表示，从而在实验样本有限的情况下实现更高效的CATE估计。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes leveraging multiple outcomes from large historical datasets to learn low-dimensional representations of high-dimensional covariates, enabling sample-efficient CATE estimation when experimental samples are limited.
